chain: reverse-spend index (SPENT_BY_TABLE) + get_output_spent_by RPC
Contributed by Ziyang (as exfer-stack) upstream to ahuman-exfer/exfer, the Exfer chain itself.
This pull request is merged.
https://github.com/ahuman-exfer/exfer/pull/21

## Why

The node currently exposes two complementary "what's at this outpoint" lookups:

- `get_address_utxos` / `get_script_utxos` — "what's spendable right now?"
- `get_transaction(tx_id)` — "what does this tx say?"

Both are O(1) because of the `UTXOS_TABLE` / `TX_INDEX_TABLE` indexes the node maintains. But the **reverse-direction** question — *given an outpoint that's no longer in the UTXO set, what transaction consumed it, and when?* — has no index behind it today.

That question shows up in a lot of places that aren't tied to any one downstream:

- **Block explorers** linking from a confirmed transaction's input back to the spending transaction.
- **Chain-history APIs / mempool dashboards** that surface "this output was spent in block N by tx X" panels.
- **Atomic-swap counterparties** verifying that their counterparty's lock output really was claimed (and which arm), without having to re-scan the chain.
- **Light-client / wallet recovery flows** confirming a known output's eventual fate after the wallet went offline.
- **Audit tooling / forensic analysis** following the spend graph forward from a given outpoint.

Without an index, every one of these has to walk forward from the spent height and scan every block's inputs for a hit. On a chain at the current tip-depth, that's a per-query cost in the seconds even for warm-cache reads, and it scales linearly with the chain growing. The cost is paid by every downstream that needs the answer, every time.

This PR adds the missing index inside the node so a single O(1) lookup answers the question once and for all callers.

## What

**One new redb table**, populated incrementally inside the node's existing atomic commits:

```
SPENT_BY_TABLE
  key:   serialize_outpoint_key(prev_tx_id, output_index)    [36 B fixed]
  value: spending_tx_id || input_index_LE || block_height_LE [44 B fixed]
```

The write path runs inside the same redb write transaction as `UTXOS_TABLE`:

- `commit_genesis_atomic` — no-op for the coinbase-only genesis (called for symmetry / forward compat).
- `commit_block_atomic` — `apply_spent_by_for_block(block)` in the same `write_txn` as `UTXOS_TABLE`.
- `commit_reorg_atomic` — `revert_spent_by_for_block` on every orphan, then `apply_spent_by_for_block` on the trigger + every promoted ancestor, all inside one `write_txn`. The table can never diverge from the canonical chain because the redb txn either lands both updates or rolls both back.

`apply_spent_by_for_block` is idempotent (re-inserting `(key, value)` overwrites with the same bytes), so an interrupted reorg or a backfill re-run is safe.

**Three new public methods** on `ChainStorage`:

```rust
pub fn get_output_spent_by(&self, prev_tx_id: &Hash256, output_index: u32)
    -> Result<Option<SpentBy>, StorageError>;
pub fn spent_by_table_is_empty(&self) -> Result<bool, redb::Error>;
pub fn build_spent_by_index_from_genesis(&self)
    -> Result<(blocks_processed: u64, inputs_indexed: u64), StorageError>;
```
